main_body: Leafy tree canopy (large round mass of greens) on a thin brown trunk with a small grass patch at the base
top_band: Canopy: rows 1-4 lighter green (L~111) at the crown, but it is a continuous leaf mass with mottled light/dark clumps and no distinct top band separated from a front face
evidence: This is an organic tree. The canopy is a rounded volume with light foliage clumps toward the top and darker clumps lower, and the trunk and grass patch below it. No receding side face is drawn and it is not a flat architectural elevation. Its shading reads as a rounded 3/4-view canopy like the Beodeul tree references, so the 3/4 contract is satisfied for an organic object.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 13 distinct colours and a median of 6 colours per tile, against about 108 per tile and 427-567 colours in the references. The canopy uses about 4 greens (dark, mid, light, highlight) in mottled clumps with no flat 5x5 areas. Outlines are tinted dark green (0% neutral). The references have far more shading steps, per-leaf highlights and varied hues, while the trunk here is a plain 2-tone brown strip and the leaf clumps are coarser. It is clearly thinner than the references, so it fails on density and shading depth.
